en: Using a wooden ramp to load heavy boxes into a truck reduces the required lifting force, preventing back injuries.
Wearing rubber-soled shoes increases friction with the floor, which prevents you from slipping and falling on wet surfaces.
Wearing a certified helmet while biking protects your brain from severe injury because gravity accelerates your fall downward.
Swallowing multiple small button magnets is extremely dangerous because they can attract each other inside the intestines and pinch tissue.
Never touching electrical switches with wet hands prevents dangerous shocks because tap water contains dissolved minerals that conduct electricity.
Looking directly at a solar eclipse without special filtered glasses can permanently burn your retina due to intense ultraviolet light.
Wearing foam earplugs at a loud rock concert protects your eardrums because sounds above 85 decibels cause permanent hearing damage.
Wearing thick silicone oven mitts prevents hand burns when holding hot pans because silicone is a poor thermal conductor.
Eating a carbohydrate-rich banana before playing basketball provides chemical energy that your body converts into kinetic energy for muscle movement.
Rubbing your cold hands together vigorously warms your skin because friction converts your kinetic energy into thermal energy.
Plugging too many high-wattage appliances into a single extension cord can start a fire by overheating the internal wires.
Using a wheelbarrow to transport heavy garden soil uses a wheel and axle to reduce the force needed, protecting your spine.
